riff.title: The first Friday roll-up, drafted
riff.message:
Tanya — you ruled the cadence, so I made the first one. This is what Friday's roll-up would look like, built from the week the graph actually holds. The bundle is for the run; this is for the week.

---

**Week of Oct 5–9 — roll-up**

**What moved**
- Reaction cadence is settled: the per-run bundle stays, and on Fridays we add one roll-up of the week — what moved, what is still open — instead of asking anyone to scroll back. (Ruled Oct 9.)
- The roll-up coexists with the bundle, it does not replace it. Tina's question is answered on the record: the bundle is for the run, the roll-up is for the week.
- A daily digest was considered and rejected — most days carry a single run and it would repeat the bundle word for word.

**What is still open**
- The cadence position is framed but its edges aren't drawn: what a light week looks like (one run, one bundle — does the roll-up just point at it?), and whether a heavy week's roll-up links back to each run's bundle or restates it.

**Why this matters (the long arc)**
This is the March problem finally getting its delivery mechanism. Back on 2026-03-10 the founding insight was that decisions made in Slack disappear into scroll-back — "Nobody updates it" — and the product thesis became: capture the decision at the moment it's made, zero extra steps. The webhook architecture ("we only process actual decisions, not every message") solved capture. This ruling solves retrieval: nobody has to scroll back, ever, at any timescale — the run for the day, the roll-up for the week.

---

One thing I'd flag: the rejection of the daily digest was reasoned from "most days carry a single run." If run volume grows, that rationale inverts — worth a line in the ruling's margin so future-us knows the rejection is load-bearing on volume, not on principle.

riff.why_no_registered_skill: clarify only asks a question about an undefined term, and nothing here is undefined; merge-suggest flags duplicate captures, and this isn't one; refract produces a lens analysis, not a made artifact; review-message is the mechanical post-save note about a person's own earlier words; review-request is a model-free position-review prompt — none of them would draft the roll-up artifact the ruling just created the need for.
